anomalies.observed: R36 has schematic value "24k" but its MPN FRC0805J240TSD and description state 24Ω. The two fields disagree by a factor of 1000.
anomalies.expected: The value and sourcing metadata should agree. In this bleeder position across VOUTP/VOUTN, 24k is the electrically sensible value; a 24Ω part would impose an excessive load if PoE voltage is present.

evidence.quote: (comp (ref "R36") (value "24k") ... (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS") ... (MPN "FRC0805J240TSD")

anomalies.impact: If assembly follows the MPN/LCSC field, a 24Ω resistor will be fitted across the PoE extraction rail instead of 24k, causing a very large load and possible overheating; if the value field is used, the BOM metadata is incorrect.

anomalies.observed: D30 pin 4 (A2) is tied directly to ESTOP_OUT, while D30 pin 2 (K2) is connected through R60 back to the same ESTOP_OUT net. The second LED has both terminals on the same net through its series resistor.
anomalies.expected: The second LED should have its anode/cathode connected between ESTOP_OUT and an opposite rail (typically GND) so that it can indicate the e-stop state.
anomalies.impact: No potential difference ever appears across the second LED, so it will never illuminate. The board loses the intended e-stop status indication from D30.

anomalies.observed: The net LED_3.3V_POWER_SW contains only the anodes of D4, D14, and D23. There is no connection to any supply rail, driver, jumper, or other source on this net.
anomalies.expected: LED anodes must be connected to a 3.3V supply or switched LED supply so that the LEDs can conduct when their cathodes are pulled low by the Ethernet/activity signals.
anomalies.impact: The three LEDs D4, D14, and D23 have floating anodes and will not light, so Ethernet link/activity and related status indications are nonfunctional.

parsed.summary: The design files contain several concrete deviations: R36 has conflicting 24k/24Ω metadata, D30's second LED is wired back to its own anode net through R60 so it can never light, and the D4/D14/D23 LED anodes sit on an undriven net. These would cause assembly and functional differences from the intended board.
